D Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph 20 JAN ZOO OPINION NO. -U— MAYOR BENJAMIN B. MAGALONG Baguio City Office of the City Mayor City Hall Loop, Baguio City Dear Mayor Magalong: S. 20Q0 This has reference to the letter you sent dated 04 November 2019, seeking for this Department's clarification on Sections 385 and 386 of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, as amended ("LGC"). In the letter dated 04 November 2019, Sections 385 and 386 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, as amended (LGC) were cited to seek clarification as to the creation, division, merging, abolition or substantial alteration of the boundary of barangays in Baguio City, a highly urbanized city. At the outset, considering the lack of context of your query in the said letter and its failure to contain sufficient particulars, this Department is unable to provide an adequate and direct explanation to address your concern regarding clarification of pertinent provisions of the LGC in relation to the to the creation, division, merging, abolition or substantial alteration of the boundary of barangays, and its application to the City of Baguio. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this Department still deems it proper to discuss the matter about creation of barangays. Accordingly, this Department would like to reiterate that the LGC, the general law applicable to all local government units and its local officials, sets the technical and political structure and mode of governance of all local governments, barangays included. Simply stated, the LGC is the basic law which must be considered by all local government units. In that regard, this Department would like to cite the relevant provisions in the LGC which provides that the creation of local government unit, such as a barangay, needs as law enacted by Congress or an ordinance passed by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan or Panlungsod concerned, to wit: SECTION 6. Authority to Create Local Government Units. — A local government unit may be created, divided, merged, abolished, or its boundaries substantially altered either by law enacted by Congress in the case of a province, city, municipality, or any other political subdivision, or by ordinance passed by the sangguniang panlalawigan or

sangguniang pan/ungsod concerned in the case of a barangay located within its territorial jurisdiction, subject to such limitations and requirements prescribed in this Code. SECTION 385. Manner of Creation. — A barangay may be created, divided, merged, abolished, or its boundary substantially altered, by law or by an ordinance of the sangguniang panla/awigan or sangguniang pan/ungsod, subject to approval by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite to be conducted by the COMELEC in the local government unit or units directly affected within such period of time as may be determined by the law or ordinance creating said barangay. In the case of the creation of barangays by the sangguniang pan/a/awigan, the recommendation of the sangguniang bayan concerned Shal/ be necessary. Furthermore, under Section 386 of the LGC, the following are the requisites for the creation of a barangay in highly urbanized cities: 1. That the territory to be created should be contiquous or physically in contact with each other. However, if the territory is composed of two or more islands, the territory need not be contiguous; 2. In cities and municipalities within Metro Manila and other metropolitan political subdivisions or highly urbanized cities. the territory has a population of at least 5 000. Such population shall be duly certified bv the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA)•, 3. That the creation of a new barangay shall not reduce the population of the mother barangay_ to less than the minimum requirement; 4. That the territorial jurisdiction of the new barangay shall be properlv identified bv metes and bounds or by more or less permanent natural boundaries. However, it is noteworthy to mention that Section 3862 also emphasized that the requirements, such as population, for the creation of a barangay, if it involves indigenous cultural minorities, may be disregarded when Congress creates the barangay. However, if a barangay is to be created either by the Sangguniang 2 SECTION 386. Requisites for Creation. — (a) xxx To enhance the delivery of basic services in the indigenous cultural communities, barangays may be created in such communities by an act Of Congress, notwithstanding the above requirement.

Panlungsod or Panlalawigan, the latter bodies cannot set aside the requirements set forth under the LGC for the creation of a barangay. Moreover, other than the passage of a law or ordinance, the LGC also requires that a plebiscite be conducted after the passage of the said law or ordinance. Otherwise stated, the residents of the barangays affected should vote if they are in favour of the creation of the new barangay, viz. : SECTION 10. Plebiscite Requirement. - No creation, division, merger, abolition, or substantial alteration of boundaries of local government units shall take effect unless approved by a majority of the votes cast in a plebiscite called for the purpose in the political unit or units directly affected. Said plebiscite shall be conducted by the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) within one hundred twenty (120) days from the date of effectivity of the law or ordinance effecting such action, unless said law or ordinance fixes another date. Hence, to recapitulate, barangays, whether tribal or not, may be created by law passed by Congress or by an ordinance passed by either the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Panlalawigan having the territorial jurisdiction thereof, as the case may be, provided that the specific requirements under the LGC and other relevant laws, such as Republic Act No. 8731 or the Indigenous Peoples Right Act, are complied with. We hope to have provided sufficient guidelines regarding your concern. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated in the letter and our appreciation of the same. Thank you. Und LLLS/32 COPY FURNISHED: MARLO L.
